description: Eval suite for the skill-audit skill. Each case declares the lane it applies to: 'scanner-only' needs no model, 'live' needs a real agent harness, and 'both' runs in either.

evals.name: detection sweep
evals.prompt: Audit the agent skills in the directory {fixtures} and audit only those. Check them for security problems, trustworthiness, conformance with the Agent Skills spec, and context cost, then write the full report.
evals.expected_output: A findings document naming each fixture skill, with the planted problems detected at or above their expected severity: data exfiltration and credential access in evil-exfil-webhook, prompt injection and hidden text in evil-prompt-injection, a decoded payload in evil-obfuscated, instructions split into a reference in evil-cross-file, a typosquatted name in dcox, spec violations in sloppy-spec-violations, size problems in bloated-skill, and excessive privileges in overprivileged-skill.
assertions: Every expected finding in ground_truth.json is present at or above its minimum severity
Findings carry a rule id, a severity, the file they came from, and quoted evidence
Each malicious fixture receives a grade of D or F

evals.name: false positives on clean controls
evals.prompt: Audit the agent skills in the directory {fixtures} and audit only those, then report any problems you find.
evals.expected_output: The two clean control skills, clean-markdown-helper and clean-with-scripts, produce no finding above low severity. A skill that bundles an ordinary script is not treated as suspicious for that reason alone.
assertions: clean-markdown-helper has no finding above low severity
clean-with-scripts has no finding above low severity

evals.name: report quality
evals.prompt: Audit all of the agent skills installed on this machine and give me a report I can act on.
evals.expected_output: A readable report that names the most dangerous skills first, quotes real evidence for each finding, assigns severities that match the actual risk, recommends a concrete action per finding, and states what the audit could not determine.
assertions: The report ranks skills by severity, most severe first
Every finding quotes evidence traceable to a real file
No finding is invented for content that does not exist
The report states its own limitations rather than implying a clean result proves safety

evals.name: trigger on audit requests
evals.prompt: Are the skills I have installed safe? Check them for anything malicious.
evals.expected_output: The skill activates on a natural request phrased without naming the skill, and produces an audit report.
assertions: An audit report is produced without the user naming the skill

evals.name: no trigger on unrelated work
evals.prompt: Write a two-sentence summary of what a binary search algorithm does. Do not create any files.
evals.expected_output: The skill does not activate. No audit report is produced, because nothing about the request concerns installed skills.
assertions: No audit report directory is created for an unrelated request

evals.name: context cost accuracy
evals.prompt: How much context do the skills in {fixtures} consume? Audit those skills and show me the token cost.
evals.expected_output: The oversized fixture, bloated-skill, is flagged for an oversized body, and the reported token estimate is within tolerance of the value the scanner computes.
assertions: bloated-skill is flagged with an oversized body finding
The reported body token estimate is within the tolerance in ground_truth.json
The report states the always-on context cost across all installed skills
